public_rationale: Provider announcements establish that LLM systems used external Python execution, web search, and other services before the post. The model was therefore one component of a broader working system. This supports the present architectural reading of partial solution. It does not establish the stronger proposition that standalone models can never become sufficient.
limitations: Tool adoption does not by itself prove necessity, failure, or a permanent capability ceiling.
The conclusion about a partial solution depends on reading it as a claim about deployed systems.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs have already resorted to using lots of external tools such as calculators and Python interpreters, and it is already clear that they are more of a partial solution than the full solution people imagine.

statement.excerpt: And LLMs themselves have already resorted to using lots of external tools like calculators and python interpreters; it is already clear that they are more of a partial solution than the full solution people imagine.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

from_speaker: already resorted to using lots of external tools
more of a partial solution than the full solution people imagine
our_interpretation: LLMs using tools refers to deployed systems in which a language model requests external computation or services.
Calculators and Python interpreters are examples; the claim does not require a separate calculator product in every system.
Partial solution is read as a present architectural claim: the language model supplies part of a broader system's capabilities.
Tool adoption alone cannot establish that tools are permanently necessary or that a standalone model could never attain general intelligence.
Already makes this a cumulative observation within the post's three-year retrospective.
criteria.support_condition: Dated deployment documentation establishes that LLM systems integrate multiple external capabilities, including executable computation, with the model acting as a component of the resulting system.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The cited capabilities were generated entirely by the language model without external execution or services, or documentation establishes the claimed complete standalone capability under a defined task scope.
